title: Geometrically reduced flat base change of ordinary alteration covers
statement: Let $S,S'$ be reduced Noetherian schemes [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $h:S'\to S$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] with geometrically reduced fibres: for every field $K$ and map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$, the scheme $S'\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$ is reduced. Use the ordinary alteration category and topology of [def-per-ordinary-alteration-topology]. For every object $T\to S$ of $\operatorname{alt}/S$, the ordinary fibre product $T\times_SS'$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is reduced and is an object of $\operatorname{alt}/S'$. If $(T_i\to S)_i$ is a finite ordinary alteration covering, then $(T_i\times_SS'\to S')_i$ is a finite ordinary alteration covering. No finite-type hypothesis on $h$ is required. In particular this applies when $h$ is regular [def-per-regular-scheme-morphism], meaning flat with geometrically regular fibres, and when $h$ is a flat finitely presented nodal curve morphism [def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres]. On any reduced Noetherian scheme $R$, the finite family of its nonempty reduced irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] is an ordinary alteration covering of $R$. The empty scheme has the empty such covering.

source.place: Expose II 1.2.3 (fourth bullet), 1.2.5--1.2.8, 2.3.1--2.3.4, printed pp.24--28, ordinary case (parameter 1), with geometrically reduced flat base change so that reduction of the products is unnecessary. Component covering: II 1.2.8 and the proper-surjective generator. The arbitrary Noetherian flat completion base change is used in VII 3.2, printed p.82.

proof.text: Fix the prime $2$ only to invoke the existing generator-base-change theorem; the underlying category $\operatorname{alt}/S$ is independent of that choice. The hypothesis on $h$ implies its finite-residue-extension reducedness hypothesis, by taking $K$ to be each such extension. That theorem therefore says that $F(T)=T\times_S S'$ is an object of $\operatorname{alt}/S'$ for every $T$, and defines a functor on all morphisms. By the object definition its source is reduced, is finite type over $S'$, and satisfies both required generic-point conditions. This proves the first assertion, including reducedness of the ordinary, unreduced fibre product. Neither the theorem nor this specialization assumes $h$ finite type.

source.place: II 1.2.2 and 1.2.3, fourth bullet; the stronger all-field reducedness assumption implies the finite-extension assumption of the cited node.

proof.text: The same theorem states that $F$ preserves the terminal object and every categorical fibre-product cone. These are assertions about the underlying alteration categories, which are identical for the ordinary and prime-to-$2$ topologies. Thus they apply here without any assertion that the categorical product is the whole ordinary scheme product. For use below, the alteration calculus identifies that categorical product with the reduced union of the dominating components of the ordinary product.

source.place: II 1.2.5--1.2.6, and flat base-change comparison of the dominant parts.

proof.text: For a jointly surjective etale family $(U_a\to T)_a$ in $\operatorname{alt}/S$, the ordinary base-change lemma gives a jointly surjective etale family over $T'=T\times_S S'$. The ordinary scheme product $U_a\times_T T'$ is canonically $U_a\times_S S'$: a map to either is precisely a pair of maps to $U_a$ and $S'$ agreeing over $S$. Its members are objects by step 1. Likewise a proper surjective generator $U\to T$ pulls back to a proper surjective map $U\times_S S'\to T'$ by proper and surjective base change. Hence $F$ sends both classes of ordinary generators to ordinary generators, without imposing any residue-degree condition on an etale cover.

source.place: II 2.1.1 at parameter 1, 2.3.1 and 2.3.4; Stacks morphisms.tex Tags 02GO (lemma-base-change-etale), 01S1 (lemma-base-change-surjective), 01W4 (lemma-base-change-proper).

proof.text: We check that the generator families are stable under categorical pullback, on either base $B=S$ or $B=S'$. For objects $U\to T\leftarrow V$, put $C=U\times_T V$. Its categorical product is $C_{\mathrm{md}}$ by the alteration calculus. If $U\to T$ is etale, the dominant-part etale comparison gives $C_{\mathrm{md}}\simeq C\times_V V_{\mathrm{md}}=C$, since the reduced maximally dominant object $V$ equals $V_{\mathrm{md}}$. The etale base-change lemma gives joint surjectivity for a whole family. If $U\to T$ is proper surjective, ordinary base change makes $C\to V$ proper surjective; the proper-surjection clause of the dominant-part theorem makes $C_{\mathrm{md}}\to V_{\mathrm{md}}=V$ proper surjective. Thus categorical pullbacks are again generators. All schemes in these dominant-part applications are finite type over the Noetherian $B$, as in the categorical-product clause of the calculus.

source.place: II 1.2.5--1.2.8 and Remark 2.3.2, verification of pullback stability of the two ordinary generator classes.

proof.text: On either alteration category form a precoverage $P$ consisting of singleton isomorphisms and all families obtained by iterated composition of the two generator classes. Precisely, use well-founded rooted trees: the children at a non-leaf vertex form a generator family or an isomorphism, and the arrows from the leaves to the root form the resulting family. Grafting trees proves composition stability. Pull a tree back along an arrow by pulling back the family at the root and then each subtree; well-founded induction and step 4 prove pullback stability. This allows arbitrary branching; no uniform bound on tree heights is assumed. Each tree family covers for the ordinary topology by well-founded induction using local character. Conversely $P$ contains the generators. Minimality therefore identifies its generated topology with the ordinary topology. The cited stable-precoverage membership theorem now says that every ordinary covering sieve contains one of these tree families.

source.place: II 2.3.1--2.3.3, explicit closure under composition; stable-precoverage membership: Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/PrecoverageToGrothendieck.lean:166--201.

proof.text: Apply $F$ to a tree family. It sends its root generator to a generator by step 3 and its singleton isomorphisms to isomorphisms. Inductively it sends each subtree family to a covering family, so local character makes the family of all image leaf composites covering. Now let $R$ be the sieve generated by the given finite covering $(T_i\to S)_i$. Step 5 supplies a tree family $(A_a\to S)_a$ contained in $R$. Each leaf arrow factors through some $T_i\to S$, so its image factors through $F(T_i)\to F(S)=S'$. The latter generated sieve therefore contains the covering image tree family and is covering by local character (or upward closure). Its index set is the original finite set of indices $i$, so this is exactly the asserted finite covering, with ordinary fibre products. This passage does not replace an ordinary cover by a prime-to-$2$ cover.

source.place: II 2.3.4, generator argument expanded using the precoverage of step 5.

proof.text: For a regular $h$, fix $s\in S$ and put $k=\kappa(s)$. By the definition of a regular morphism, the scheme-theoretic fibre over $s$ remains regular after every finite field extension $E/k$. Its regular local rings are domains by the cited theorem, hence reduced (a nilpotent in a domain is zero); so the stalkwise definition makes that fibre reduced. For an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of the fibre over $k$, its pullback after $E/k$ has coordinate ring $A\otimes_kE$, which is therefore reduced. The finite-purely-inseparable test gives reducedness of $A\otimes_kK$ for every field extension $K/k$. These affine pullbacks cover the scalar-extended fibre; the affine reducedness and open-cover criteria show it is reduced. Every field-valued point factors through the residue field of its image, so fibre-product associativity gives the all-field hypothesis of the item. Flatness is part of regularity. This argument does not require arbitrary scalar-extended fibres to remain Noetherian regular schemes.

source.place: Stacks algebra.tex Tag 00NP, lemma-regular-domain; Tag 030V, lemma-geometrically-reduced-finite-purely-inseparable-extension; properties.tex Tag 02IT; schemes.tex Tags 01J2, 01I4 and 01JQ.

proof.text: For the nodal case take a point $s$ of $S$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(s)$. Finite presentation gives a finite-type geometric fibre. Its nonsmooth closed points have completed local rings $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ by the specified nodal-geometric-fibre condition. The cited nodal closed-point theorem applies even when the completed-ring isomorphisms are only ring isomorphisms, and gives reducedness of this geometric fibre; it needs no extra equidimensionality or nonemptiness assumption. The algebraic-closure test then says the fibre over $\kappa(s)$ is geometrically reduced. Every field-valued point of $S$ factors through the residue field of its image; associativity of fibre products identifies its fibre with a scalar extension of this fibre. Thus the all-field reducedness hypothesis holds. Flatness is already assumed, so steps 1--6 apply.

source.place: Stacks curves.tex Tag 0E37, lemma-facts-about-nodal-curves (reduced completed local rings), with the one-field version cited here; varieties.tex Tag 035X, lemma-geometrically-reduced.

proof.text: Finally fix a reduced Noetherian $R$. The component-cover clause of the alteration calculus, applied with the prime $2$, states that its finite family of reduced irreducible components covers for the prime-to-$2$ topology. That topology is contained in the ordinary one: a prime-to-$2$ decomposed etale generator is a jointly surjective etale family, and a proper surjective maximally prime-to-$2$ finite generator is a proper surjective map in the same category. Thus every such generator covers for the ordinary topology, and the minimality in its definition gives the inclusion of topologies. The component family is therefore an ordinary covering. Components are nonempty by the irreducibility convention. When $R$ is empty there are no components, and the empty etale family is jointly surjective onto it, so its empty generated sieve covers by the ordinary generator definition.

source.place: II 1.2.8, 2.1.1 and 2.3.1--2.3.3; component cover by the finite proper component coproduct and its open summands, as recorded in the cited calculus.
